items.body: Defenseman skating again after sustaining skull fracture during preseason game ST. PAUL, Minn. -- Brock Faber practiced with the Minnesota Wild for the second straight day on Friday, and the defenseman understands the fractured skull he sustained during a preseason game "could have been a lot worse." Faber returned to the ice this week after recovering from a skull fracture he sustained during a preseason game against the Dallas Stars on Sept. 25, when he was hit in the head with a shot during the second period. The puck hit him around the ear area that isn't protected by the helmet. "It could have been a lot worse if, one, if I got hit harder in that spot, and two, if I didn’t get the medical attention that I did," he said. "I'm so glad to just put it in the past. It's so good to be back. "If it would have got me a couple centimeters lower, it just would have hit me in the ear and I'd had to maybe get a couple stitches on my ear. If it would have hit me a couple inches or centimeters higher, it hits me in the helmet and I'm fine. The area where I got hit, only a puck could fit there. And it just so happened that it hit me right there." Faber has added plastic ear guards to his helmet as he ramps up his skating and physical fitness toward making his season debut. That timeline is undetermined, although Wild coach John Hynes said Faber is expected to travel on the three-game road trip that starts at the Montreal Canadiens on Tuesday. Faber started working out again about a week ago and is ramping up his conditioning and strength after about a month off. items.body: Linus Ullmark has been removed from the team's injured reserve list and placed back on the roster on Sunday, signalling he may be ready to return to play. In a corresponding move, Jonas Johansson was sent back down to the AHL. Ullmark left a game against the Florida Panthers on Oct. 21 with a lower-body strain after he stopped a hard shot from former teammate Brady Tkachuk. The goaltender was expected to miss one to two weeks with injury. It marked the second time the 33-year-old has been pulled from the net because of injury this season. Ullmark has a 7-1-0 record on the season with a 1.33 goals-against average and a .945 save percentage. The Senators (11-6-1) get back to action Tuesday against the Washington Capitals.

items.title: Report: Leafs call up D Cole McWard, send F Vinni Lettieri to AHL
items.body: The Toronto Maple Leafs added some defensive depth to the roster after Morgan Rielly left Saturday's loss with an injury. Defenceman Cole McWard was called up from the Toronto Marlies of the AHL, while forward Vinni Lettieri was sent down in a corresponding move, The Hockey News' David Alter reported on Sunday. McWard, 25, has spent some time up with the big club this season, but has yet to see game action. In seven contests with the Marlies, he has four assists and is a plus-3. The right-shot blueliner joined Toronto on a two-year deal in the off-season and comes with nine games of NHL experience, tallying one goal. Lettieri, meanwhile, played in eight games for the Maple Leafs this season, totalling one goal. However, the veteran forward has spent much of his time in Toronto in the AHL, appearing in five games this season after 55 last year while helping the Marlies win the Calder Cup.

items.title: Capitals’ Wilson won’t face supplemental discipline for hit on Vilmanis
items.summary: The Washington Capitals’ Tom Wilson won’t face further discipline after his actions on Saturday night.
items.body: The Washington Capitals ' Tom Wilson won't face further discipline after his actions on Saturday. Wilson delivered a hard hit to the back of Florida Panthers ' Sandis Vilmanis in the first period that sent the forward headfirst into the area where the glass meets the boards. Vilmanis left the game and did not return, and Wilson received a major penalty for boarding and a game misconduct for the play. After speculation about whether Wilson would face a hearing for the hit, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported Sunday that he's hearing the Capitals' star will not face supplemental discipline. Panthers coach Paul Maurice said after the game that Florida was waiting on more information about Vilmanis' condition. “Getting looked at by another doctor tomorrow," he said. "But probably we’ll have to wait until we get him back to see our guys before we have a real good idea, get some imaging.” Wilson has been suspended several times during his 14-year career. He was given 20 games for a blindside hit to the head in 2018, a ban later reduced to 14 games on appeal after he had already served 16. He received a seven-game suspension for boarding Boston’s Brandon Carlo with head contact in 2021 and six games in 2024 for a stick to the face of Toronto Maple Leafs forward Noah Gregor. The 22-year-old Vilmanis had his first career two-goal game Wednesday night when Florida beat Chicago.

Wilson was suspended for six games . The 32-year-old winger’s last hit-related suspension came on March 6, 2021, when he boarded Bruins defenseman Brandon Carlo . items.summary: Defenceman Kevin Bahl is set to undergo season-ending surgery to repair a ruptured Achilles tendon, the team announced Sunday.
items.body: The Calgary Flames have lost a piece on their blue line for the remainder of the year. Defenceman Kevin Bahl is set to undergo season-ending surgery to repair a ruptured Achilles tendon, the team announced Sunday. "A terrible break for a guy that I would consider our best player up to this point in the season," head coach Ryan Huska said of Bahl's injury. "Unfortunately, sometimes things happen, and because of that, we're losing a really good player for the rest of the year." Bahl suffered the injury on Friday prior to warmups ahead of the game against the Anaheim Ducks and was promptly ruled out. Joel Hanley entered the lineup in his place. The 26-year-old had played in all 16 of Calgary's games this season, averaging 21:56 of ice time per night while collecting one goal and one assist. Playing in his seventh NHL season, the New Westminster, B.C., native has picked up 12 goals and 53 assists in 313 games split between the Flames and New Jersey Devils. Bahl was acquired by the Flames in 2024 as part of the trade that sent Jacob Markstrom to New Jersey.

items.title: Penguins’ Sidney Crosby moves to sixth all-time in NHL scoring
items.summary: Crosby recorded his 1,772nd career point and passed Marcel Dionne for sixth on the NHL’s all-time list.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Sidney Crosby moved into sole possession of sixth place on the NHL’s all-time points list after he scored twice to help the Pittsburgh Penguins win 5-2 over the Los Angeles Kings Saturday night. Crosby passed Hockey Hall of Famer Marcel Dionne with his 1,772nd point after he deflected the puck past Kings goaltender Darcy Kuemper in the second period. He scored an empty netter to seal the win for Pittsburgh. The 39-year-old now has six goals and six assists for 12 points in 17 games this season. In 2025-26, Crosby passed Mario Lemieux and Steve Yzerman for eighth and seventh all-time in points, respectively. He now needs 26 points to pass Hall of Famer Ron Francis for fifth on the all-time list. Across 21 NHL seasons, Crosby has 660 goals and 1,113 assists for 1,773 points in 1,437 career regular-season games. He has hit the 100-point mark in six seasons and recorded at least 50 assists in a season 12 times. During that time, he’s broken the 100-point mark six times, recorded at least 50 assists 12 times, hit the 30-goal mark 13 times and has averaged more than a point-per-game in every season of his career. Crosby also has 72 goals and 134 assists for 206 points in 186 career playoff games. He captained the Penguins to three Stanley Cup championships in 2009, 2016 and 2017, and helped them reach the Stanley Cup Final in 2008. He also won the Conn Smythe Trophy in both 2016 and 2017. Crosby has twice won each of the Hart Trophy, the Art Ross Trophy, the Maurice “Rocket” Richard Trophy and the Ted Lindsay Award.

items.body: EDMONTON -- Ryan Nugent-Hopkins sustained an apparent head injury 45 seconds into the second period of a 4-2 win for the Edmonton Oilers against the Vancouver Canucks at Rogers Place on Saturday and did not return to the game. The forward was hit on the side of the head with an attempted shoot-in by Oilers defenseman Ryan Shea. Nugent-Hopkins left the ice immediately and did not return. “I don’t think he is (going to miss much time), actually,” Edmonton coach Mike Babcock said after the game. “Initially, you’re worried about a broken jaw and they did an assessment on that. Just knowing our medical guys, there will probably be more assessments tomorrow. But I just shook his hand, he was in the hallway and seemed to be doing OK.” The 33-year-old has 11 points (four goals, seven assists) in nine games. He missed the first nine games of the season with a lower-body injury and made his season debut in a 6-5 shootout win against the Carolina Hurricanes on Oct. 22. Nugent-Hopkins broke the Oilers all-time games played record in a 4-3 shootout loss at the New Jersey Devils on Tuesday, playing in his 1,038th game. Rather than creating offense, Matthew Schaefer and Luke Hughes exchanged punches late in the second period of their heated Metropolitan Division rivalry matchup between the New York Islanders and New Jersey Devils . Just kind of grabbing each other.” The heated disagreement is very out of character for both players, as neither the 19-year-old Schaefer nor the 23-year-old Hughes has ever gotten into an NHL fight. items.body: Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” Video review determined that Los Angeles’ Alex Laferriere preceded the puck into the offensive zone and was in an off-side position prior to the goal. According to Rule 38.9, “The standard for overturning the call in the event of a “GOAL” call on the ice is that the NHL Situation Room, after reviewing any and all available replays and consulting with the On-Ice Official(s), determines that one or more Players on the attacking team preceded the puck into the attacking zone prior to the goal being scored and that, as a result, the play should have been stopped for an “Off-Side” infraction; where this standard is met, the goal will be disallowed.” The clock is reset to show 4:29 (15:31 elapsed time), when the off-side infraction occurred.

items.title: Oilers’ Connor McDavid ties Adam Oates with assists in 18 consecutive games
items.body: Connor McDavid is taking a real run at one of Wayne Gretzky's records. The Edmonton Oilers star notched an assist in his 18th consecutive game to start the season on Saturday. McDavid set up Mattias Ekholm for the first goal of the night in the first period against the visiting Vancouver Canucks. McDavid moved into a tie with Adam Oates (1992-93, Boston Bruins) for second on the NHL list of most consecutive games with an assist. Another Hall of Famer, Gretzky, owns the record with 23 games in a row with an assist, set in 1990-91 with the Oilers. If McDavid can keep his run going, he'd be able to tie and break the record in Florida and Tampa Bay on Nov. 17 and 19. Mattias Ekholm and Jason Dickinson also scored for the Oilers (12-3-3) who snapped a two-game losing skid. The Oilers are 10-0-2 when they score first this season. He now leads the league with 10 goals, 37 assists and 47 points. The Oilers captain matched Adam Oates for the second-longest assist streak in NHL history behind only Wayne Gretzky’s 23 games set in 1990-91. Edmonton took a 3-1 lead four minutes into the final frame as their potent power play struck when McDavid sent it across to Draisaitl and he unleashed his patented one-timer for his 15th of the season. The Devils erased a two-goal deficit in the third period, capped by Hamilton’s power-play goal with 6:18 remaining in regulation. Jack Hughes curled around the net before finding Hamilton in the slot for the tying goal. Evangelista started the comeback when he pulled New Jersey within a goal at 6:08 of the third period. The Islanders took a 2-1 lead after the first period. Duclair opened the scoring with less than five minutes remaining, Rodrigues tied it 17 seconds later and Schaefer put New York back ahead with his fifth goal of the season. Chisholm tied the score at 2 just 4:42 into the second period when Jesper Bratt fired a shot off the end boards that took an awkward bounce around the net, allowing Chisholm to bury the rebound. items.body: The Montreal Canadiens likely will get a big boost late in the 2025-26 season, even if they don't do anything huge at the trade deadline. Top prospect Michael Hage (Michigan, NCAA) and second-round pick Alexander Zharovsky (Salavat Yulaev Ufa, KHL) are expected to be available to play for the Canadiens late this season after their respective campaigns conclude, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported on Saturday Headlines . Hage, who opted to return for his third year at Michigan after considering making the jump to the pro ranks last off-season, leads the NCAA in scoring with four goals and 16 assists for second-ranked Michigan. Last year, Hage, 20, led the world junior championship in scoring with two goals and 13 assists in seven games for bronze medal-winning Canada. The NCAA season wraps up April 10 with the national final. That's the same day Montreal ends its regular season, so it's possible the Canadiens would have to wait until the playoffs to have Hage as a possible option. The 19-year-old Zharovsky, also a forward, has six goals and 12 assists in 23 KHL games this season. The Canadiens picked him in the second round (34th overall) of the 2025 draft.

items.title: Trade noise getting louder around Blues’ Binnington
items.body: Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported that he's "starting to hear some noise" around the St. Louis Blues goaltender during the "Saturday Headlines" segment of Rogers Saturday Night Hockey. Binnington, 33, is an unrestricted free agent at the end of this season with a $6 million salary and a 10-team no-trade list. He has lost the starting job to Joel Hofer this season and made only five starts so far. In those five starts, Binnington has a 1-3-1 record with an .851 save percentage and a 4.27 goals-against average. The 10-year NHL veteran won a Stanley Cup with the Blues in 2019 and started for Canada at both the 4 Nations Face-Off and the 2026 Winter Olympics in Milan.

items.body: Register Login Mammoth’s Nate Schmidt Out Day-To-Day By Gabriel Foley | at November 7, 2026 7:34 pm The Utah Mammoth will need to switch up their blue-line ahead of Saturday’s game against the Ottawa Senators. Nate Schmidt will be held out of the matchup due to a day-to-day, upper-body injury. Schmidt only played in four minutes of Utah’s Thursday loss to the Montreal Canadiens. He took a hard hit from Canadiens’ forward Nick Suzuki in one of his final shifts and was in noticeable pain in subsequent shifts. Utah recalled Gregor Biber on Friday. The 20 year old will sit out of Saturday’s matchup in favor of Artyom Duda, who has no points and a minus-three through the first two games of his NHL career. The Mammoth are already facing an injury to John Marino , who fell out of the lineup on October 17th with an upper-body injury. Nick DeSimone has filled in for Marino’s hole on the right-side – though Biber is on the cusp of his NHL debut should Utah want to replace either Duda or DeSimone. Like with Marino, the Mammoth will have no immediate replacement for Schmidt’s impact. The 35 year old continues to do it all – with four points, 14 shot blocks, and 20 hits through 17 games this season. Schmidt has averaged 19 minutes of ice time per game, continuing a trend that began with his first season in Utah last year. The Mammoth will lean on rookies – either Duda or Biber – to make up for that two-way presence until Schmidt is back to full health.

items.title: Oilers activate Zach Hyman, Devon Levi off IR
items.summary: Both Hyman and Levi have been out of the lineup for approximately two weeks due to various injuries.
items.body: Hyman, 34, was injured during a game against the Detroit Red Wings last month. He appeared to hit his head against the glass and fell to the ice, then required help to the dressing room from the Oilers’ training staff. Hyman’s injury comes soon after he missed more than two weeks due to an injury sustained during Edmonton’s regular-season opener against the Canucks. He missed six games then returned to the lineup Oct. 17 against the Utah Mammoth . Through six games, Hyman has one goal and is averaging 17:56 of ice time. Now in his 12th NHL season, the Toronto native has 262 goals and 234 assists for 496 points in 717 regular-season games with the Oilers and Toronto Maple Leafs . He scored a career-high 54 goals with Edmonton in 2023-24. Hyman, a 2010 fifth-round pick for the Florida Panthers , also has 42 goals and 33 assists for 75 points in 106 career Stanley Cup Playoff games. He was part of the Oilers’ back-to-back Stanley Cup Final runs in 2024 and 2025, and scored a league-leading 16 goals during the postseason in 2024. Meanwhile, Levi posted a 6-1-0 record with an .887 save percentage (SV%) and 3.11 goals against average (GAA). In 46 career NHL games, the native of Dollard-des-Ormeaux, Que., is 23-18-2 with an .893 SV% and 3.26 GAA with the Oilers and Buffalo Sabres . Levi, a seventh-round pick for the Florida Panthers in 2020, has appeared in 120 regular-season AHL games with the Rochester Americans across three seasons. He’s posted a 64-39-22 record with a .914 SV% and 2.52 GAA.

Kyrou, a Toronto native, picked Justin Bieber’s 2015 hit “What Do You Mean?” Bieber also hails from Toronto. The song was one of the biggest hits of Bieber’s career, becoming his first tune to reach No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100. The track features a ticking-clock beat and a distinctive, high-pitched synthesizer melody that sounds like a flute. That instrumental hook, which bounces around the song’s chorus, could make for a particularly memorable goal song. Its upbeat rhythm, instantly recognizable melody, and playful electronic sounds seem tailor-made for a hockey arena, especially with thousands of fans cheering along. Kyrou’s goal song comes a day after RMNB’s Katie’s Adler asked Kyrou why the team’s default “Kickstart My Heart” by Mötley Crüe was still being used as his goal song. “I had one, but [the team] said I couldn’t do it,” Kyrou said Friday. Kyrou initially chose “Janice STFU” by his “hometown boy” Drake, but the Capitals presumably deemed it wasn’t appropriate for a crowd of all ages, leaving him unsure what to pick for the first month of the season. Arniel did not provide a timeline for Salomonsson’s return and asked fans to respect the young defender’s privacy at this time. Salomonsson was a healthy scratch for Thursday’s win over the Vancouver Canucks and sat out of Saturday’s practice with what was initially believed to be an illness per NHL.com’s Mitchell Clinton . It has been a rocky season for the 22-year-old Salomonsson. He didn’t make his season debut until October 25th, missing the start of the year while recovering from a shoulder surgery performed in April. Salomonsson has struggled since returning to the lineup. He has recorded no scoring, a minus-five, and four penalty minutes in six games – while Winnipeg has combined for a 1-5-0 record in those appearances. Arniel has continued to lean on the young defender despite those struggles, deploying him for 18:20 a game on average. That’s an uptick from Salomonsson’s usage in his rookie season last year – which was marked by five points and 17:58 in average ice time through 32 games. Winnipeg will continue to roll out forward-and-defender Tyrel Bauer on their blue line in Salomonsson’s absence. Bauer is playing through the first games of his NHL career and has two points in 11 appearances this season.

items.summary: The New York Rangers have mutually agreed to terminate the contract of goalie James Reimer on Saturday. But while this is likely the end of Reimer's NHL career, his longevity is to be admired. Even the best goalies end their NHL careers in a non-ideal manner.

The latest example of that is journeyman netminder James Reimer. The veteran goalie was placed on waivers for the purpose of contract termination by the New York Rangers on Saturday, mutually agreeing to part ways off his one-year contract. items.title: ‘Extremely grateful’: Price, Bergeron headline 2026 Hockey Hall of Fame class
items.body: TORONTO — Carey Price spent a lot of his youth on the road and in the air. Growing up in a remote part of British Columbia, that's what chasing his hockey dream required. When the phone rang in June to announce he would be joining the game's greats, Price was fittingly in a familiar situation — driving. "I was on my way to go visit my grandmother at the hospital," recalled the former Montreal Canadiens goaltender. "Hockey Hall of Fame came up with my caller ID in my truck, so pretty excited about that. Got to spend the rest of the day with my grandmother, who made a recovery. Price had plenty of those in the NHL and with Canada on the international stage. Now he will share another one Monday with the rest of the hall's 2026 class. The netminder headlines this year's inductees alongside Patrice Bergeron, Pekka Rinne, Keith Tkachuk and Cindy Curley in the player category set to be enshrined Monday. Brian Burke will go in as a builder. "A long road to get to this point," Price, who starred in Montreal for all 15 of his NHL seasons and will enter the hall in his second year of eligibility, said Saturday. "I'm just extremely thankful for that journey and everything that I learned along the way — not only in hockey but in life." The No. 5 pick at the 2005 draft, Price won the Hart Trophy as league MVP and the Vezina Trophy as its top goaltender in 2015. The 39-year-old from Anahim Lake, B.C., finished with a 361-261-79 record, .917 save percentage, 2.51 goals-against average and 49 shutouts across 712 regular-season games in a career that was, at times, hampered by injury. Price had even better big-moment numbers before a knee issue forced him to stop playing beyond the 2021-22 campaign. items.body: The Winnipeg Jets appear to be getting their No. 1 defenceman back soon. Morrissey didn't speak to the media after the skate but head coach Scott Arniel said, "He’s getting closer." “That was the first time that we really got him ramped up," Arniel added without committing to Morrissey playing Sunday against the Lightning. "I’m not hiding anything. We’ve still got to get to see how this went after today’s practice. That decision won’t get made (yet). That full lineup won’t be (known) until (Sunday)." The Jets have missed Morrissey in the lineup and sit seventh in the Central Division with a 6-8-3 record. items.summary: Jet Greaves suddenly seems like a prime candidate to ascend to the blue-paint throne for his home nation. And now that he is armed with some financial security and the starting gig in the Columbus net, he’s truly cleared for his NHL takeoff.
items.body: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Heir Canada: Is Jet Greaves The Next Goaltender To Take The Reins For Team Canada? Carol Schram Partner Nov 7, 2026 8:19 PM Published Nov 7, 2026 8:19 PM Jet Greaves suddenly seems like a prime candidate to ascend to the blue-paint throne for his home nation. And now that he is armed with some financial security and the starting gig in the Columbus net, he’s truly cleared for his NHL takeoff. When international best-on-best hockey returned at the 4 Nations Face-Off and the Milan Olympics, fans in the Great White North came face-to-face with the stark realization that Hockey Canada didn’t have a superstar netminder who could uphold the elite standards set by past Olympic gold medallists Carey Price, Roberto Luongo or Martin Brodeur. Could the nation’s hopes for the 2028 World Cup of Hockey and even the 2030 Olympics therefore rest on the shoulders of an undrafted late-bloomer who checks in at just six-foot and 190 pounds? Jet Greaves made his full-time NHL debut last season at 24, then made a strong case for himself in his first national-team showing at May’s World Championship in Switzerland. Over eight games, he allowed just 15 goals and recorded a .920 save percentage. “When you’re growing up playing hockey in Canada, one of your biggest dreams is to wear the Maple Leaf on your chest,” he said. “To be able to do that for the first time was super special.” More Videos The World Championship followed Greaves’ stellar campaign with the Columbus Blue Jackets , where he established himself as his team’s No. 1 with a record of 26-19-9 to go along with a 2.60 goals-against average and .908 SP. He also had some of the best advanced stats in the league, including the ninth-best goals saved above expected, per moneypuck.com .

Wilson was ejected 8:55 into the first period after boarding Panthers forward Sandis Vilmanis from behind. The play occurred as the Panthers tried to work the puck out of the zone. Vilmanis, set up at the half wall, pivoted to send a backhanded pass up the ice. As he did, Wilson hit him directly in the numbers, and his head slammed into the rim around the boards. Vilmanis stayed down for several minutes before being helped off the ice. Officials initially whistled a five-minute major on Wilson to review video replays. Upon a quick look at an iPad, the referees then confirmed the call on the ice and ejected Wilson from the game. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images Well, it’s been a while since we’ve had to write something like this. During a matchup between the Washington Capitals and Florida Panthers on Saturday afternoon, Capitals forward Tom Wilson was ejected after boarding Panthers defenseman Sandis Vilmanis. The incident came a little before the halfway mark of the opening period in the U.S. capital. As Vilmanis was trying to move the puck out of the Florida zone, Wilson came from his side, but ended up drilling the Latvian blueliner into the sideboards from behind. Vilmanis went down to the Panthers’ dressing room following the hit. Wilson was given a five-minute major for boarding and a game misconduct. While it’s too early to tell whether his actions will result in any additional consequences, Wilson is far from unfamiliar with supplemental discipline. The 32-year-old has been suspended six times by the NHL Department of Player Safety, including three times during the 2017-18 season, and fined on five other occasions. Wilson has tried to keep his nose clean lately, as he hasn’t been fined or suspended since April 2025. The Toronto native earned a reputation for being a dirty player, but as he has grown older, he has tried to mold his game into more of an effective power forward, rather than a brute force. Yet, he’s registered at least 100 points in each of the past three seasons, though he hasn’t come close to challenging his career-high 187 points, which came during that 2017-18 campaign. In 14 games with Washington so far this season, Wilson has scored two goals and three assists for five points. His 45 penalty minutes put him second in the NHL behind Boston Bruins defender Nikita Zadorov.

items.summary: Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid wasn't too pleased about the hit he took into the net from Anaheim Ducks defenseman Drew Helleson. But is McDavid's response a bit of an overreaction?
items.body: Perry Nelson-Imagn Images Perry Nelson-Imagn Images Did Oilers' McDavid Overreact To Helleson And Ducks Incident? Adam Proteau Partner Nov 7, 2026 6:00 PM Published Nov 7, 2026 6:00 PM Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid wasn't too pleased about the hit he took into the net from Anaheim Ducks defenseman Drew Helleson. But is McDavid's response a bit of an overreaction? For the most part, in his Hockey Hall of Fame-level career, Edmonton Oilers superstar center Connor McDavid has been a cool, calm, unflappable icon. So it’s rare to see him get angry – at least, not outside of the Oilers’ dressing room. So it was a little out of character to see McDavid going off on Anaheim Ducks defenseman Drew Helleson after he drove McDavid into the Ducks’ net. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Nick Turchiaro-Imagn Images Some promising news for a Toronto Maple Leafs team that needs a jolt. When speaking to the media, Maple Leafs head coach Jim Hiller announced that forward John Tavares will be in the lineup on Saturday night, when the team plays host to the Montreal Canadiens. Tavares has missed the last nine games due to a lower-body injury that knocked him out of a game against the Buffalo Sabres on Oct. 15. During that time, Toronto went on a four-game win streak, but has slipped over the past week, going 5-4-0 during the former captain’s absence. The Toronto native had been showing signs that he could come back soon, as he was taking reps on the Leafs’ top power-play unit during practice on Friday. One thing that will be different is that Tavares won’t be in his normal position. As he’s been closing in on a full bill of health, No. 91 started taking reps on the wing, playing on the left side of Toronto’s second line, centered by Nick Paul with William Nylander on the right wing. Prior to his injury, Tavares had been one of the team’s consistent scorers through the opening weeks of the 2026-27 campaign. In seven appearances, the 36-year-old has scored two goals and five assists for seven points, with a plus/minus of -5 while averaging 16:31 of ice time. Tavares entered the new campaign looking to make the most of his time with his hometown team, after rumors swirled that he might not return to the Leafs, even after he posted back-to-back 30-goal seasons. Yet, the team re-signed the former London Knight to a four-year contract in June, with the deal carrying an AAV of $4.38 million . items.summary: Following a ruling last week from the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) to reinstate Russia to international hockey competitions, the IIHF stated on Saturday that, while it disagrees with the ruling, it is taking the steps required by the CAS’s decision regarding possible reimplementation.
items.body: The IIHF has come to a decision regarding Russian and Belarusian participation in upcoming tournaments. Following a ruling last week from the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) to reinstate Russia to international hockey competitions, the IIHF stated on Saturday that, while it disagrees with the ruling, it is taking the steps required by the CAS's decision regarding possible reimplementation. "While the IIHF continues to disagree with the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport concerning Russian participation in IIHF Championships, we are taking the necessary steps required by the CAS ruling and reviewing what conditions would need to be met to safeguard our Championships, protect the organization's financial stability and secure the long-term future of international ice hockey," the IIHF said in its statement. "The IIHF must work within the applicable framework while upholding its responsibility to preserve international competition and protect the sport as a whole. "The IIHF is therefore exploring all available avenues, including opening discussions with all affected MNAs (Member National Associations), including the Russian Ice Hockey Federation, to identify a constructive way forward that serves the interests of global ice hockey." Last week on Friday, the CAS overturned an exclusion of Russian participation in international ice hockey tournaments, put in place since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The IIHF has opposed Russia's immediate reinstatement, citing security, logistical and competitive concerns, while several European hockey federations have said their teams would refuse to face Russia. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Minnesota Wild made history Friday night, becoming the fastest team in NHL history to reach 1,000 regular-seaon wins as they defeated the San Jose Sharks 4-1. Minnesota was led by Kirill Kaprizov on Friday, who scored his league-leading 16th goal and added three assists. The forward has five goals and eight assists for 13 points during a seven-game point streak. Defenseman Quinn Hughes had a goal and two assists in the win. The Wild accomplished the feat in 1,995 games played, which beat the previous mark held by the Philadelphia Flyers who did it in 2,018 games. In January 2025 , the Nashville Predators did it in 2,020 games. The Wild are now 12-3-3 and possess the best record in the Western Conference and the second-best mark in the NHL . Meanwhile, the Sharks are 7-10-1 through their first 18 games of 2026-27. Minnesota entered the league as an expansion franchise in 2000-01. They reached the Western Conference Final in just their third season, but have not reached since. Mikko Koivu, who served as captain for 11 seasons, holds multiple franchise records, including the most regular-season games played (1,028) assists (504) and points (709). Meanwhile, Kaprizov is the Wild’s all-time franchise leader with 246 goals. Now in his seventh NHL season, he has 259 assists and 505 points in 415 career games.

items.summary: As delighted as Johnny Bower was to be inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame a half-century ago this year, the Toronto Maple Leafs legend was probably even happier for the goalies who were enshrined before and after him.
items.body: Legendary goalie, enshrined 50 years ago, won Cup with Maple Leafs four times As delighted as Johnny Bower was to be inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame a half-century ago this year, the Toronto Maple Leafs legend was probably even happier for the goalies who were enshrined before and after him. There was something that Bower especially enjoyed about his pads-wearing lodge brothers being joined together in this celebrated fraternity after they’d faced the final shot of their careers. Bower was the 25th of 44 goalies to be inducted into the Hall of Fame, a number that soon will grow to 46 with the inductions on Monday of Carey Price and Pekka Rinne, respectively of the Montreal Canadiens and Nashville Predators. Johnny Bower awaits a shot during a game at Toronto’s Maple Leaf Gardens. Bower died of pneumonia at age 93 on Dec. 26, 2017, having been a hugely popular presence on the red carpet at Brookfield Place for many years. Unfailingly humble, he was almost embarrassed when he was stopped for a photo or a chat on his way into the induction ceremony, and so modest was he that he sometimes needed to be talked into attending the gala event. Bower was elected to the shrine 50 years ago as a member of the Class of 1976, inducted with rugged defenseman Bill Quackenbush and members of the Builder category Jack Gibson, Philip Ross and William Wirtz. “This is really wonderful,” he said upon being elected. “It’s a great honor. It’s nice to know your name will be on the honor roll. I didn’t expect to get in this soon (six years after his final game).” Boston Bruins defenseman Bill Quackenbush, here in 1955, and Toronto Maple Leafs goalie Johnny Bower, in 1965, were the two players inducted in the Hockey Hall of Fame’s Class of 1976. items.body: Register Login Mammoth Recall Gregor Biber, Place Kailer Yamamoto On IR By Brian La Rose | at November 6, 2026 9:00 pm With Nate Schmidt suffering an upper-body injury on Thursday in Montreal, the Mammoth have made a pair of roster moves to get another blueliner on their active roster. The team announced ( Twitter link ) that they’ve recalled blueliner Gregor Biber from AHL Tucson. To make room on the roster, winger Kailer Yamamoto was placed on injured reserve. Biber was a fourth-round pick by Utah in 2024, going 98th overall. He becomes the first player from their draft class that year to receive an NHL recall. The Austria native made the move to play in Sweden in his draft year, playing in Rogle’s junior system. He then moved up to the SHL level, getting into 88 games over the last two seasons, recording just three goals and two assists in the two campaigns combined. Still, the Mammoth liked enough of what they saw to sign Biber to a three-year, entry-level contract back in May. The 20-year-old has had a decent start to his playing career in North America, notching three assists and 10 penalty minutes in his first 11 games with the Roadrunners. He will likely serve as the seventh defender behind Artem Duda until Schmidt is able to return. As for Yamamoto, he is dealing with an upper-body injury that has cost him a little more than a week so far despite the original day-to-day designation. His placement is retroactive to October 29th, meaning that he’s eligible to be activated at any time. Before being sidelined, the 28-year-old was off to a promising start with four goals and three assists in his first nine games.

items.title: Blue Jackets’ Sean Monahan exits vs. Sabres with lower-body injury
items.body: The Columbus Blue Jackets lost Sean Monahan to an injury during Friday's game against the Buffalo Sabres. Monahan was forced to exit in the second period after blocking a shot from Sabres defenceman Rasmus Dahlin while on the penalty kill. The veteran was in visible pain on the play and limped his way to the bench once the puck went down the ice. Monahan had logged 11:06 of ice time and recorded an assist on Kent Johnson's first-period marker before being sent to the locker room. The 32-year-old centre entered Friday with one goal and four assists through the first 14 games of Columbus's season. A veteran of 14 NHL campaigns, Monahan had 13 goals and 23 assists over 78 games for the Blue Jackets in 2025-26.

items.summary: The root of Elias Pettersson’s resurgence through 18 games is the healthier environment around the Canucks and the better headspace he brought into training camp.
items.body: EDMONTON – There really isn’t a chicken-or-egg conundrum about what may be the rebirth of Elias Pettersson as an impactful player. He doesn’t feel good because he’s playing better. He’s playing better because he feels good. Of course, both of those things are true. But the root of Pettersson’s resurgence through the first 18 games of this National Hockey League season is a healthier environment around the Vancouver Canucks and the better headspace the Swedish centre brought into training camp after two years in which he was like a hologram many nights. “For sure, I definitely feel a difference,” Pettersson told Sportsnet in a quiet conversation after Friday’s practice in Edmonton. “I mean, I wasn't true to myself these last two years. But this summer, the end of last season, I started working with a mental coach and, honestly, that's been game-changing for me — just to be clear on where to put my focus. Obviously, I feel like myself, but better. I know there's still growth that I want to do, but it's definitely been a huge difference for me. “I mean, (team) results don't show it, but I think the environment and everything for everyone is better. I don't like to talk about the past, but just the environment they’ve created, it's good. I've seen the difference.” The environment, and what it could mean for Pettersson, is something general manager Ryan Johnson has talked about — and cultivated — since he was hired in May to become the Canucks’ new general manager and chief architect of the biggest rebuild in franchise history. Now, he's receiving the Foster Hewitt Memorial Award "for outstanding contributions as a hockey broadcaster."
